This game kinda sucks, it's the worst RE since RE6. I'd still rather play this than 6, but jeez. The approach to the two player character situation is interesting, but it feels incomplete; it feels a bit like only getting half of two different games. Leon's campaign is verging into RE6-levels of wackiness and action, and is a major unwanted detour from the survival horror direction of 7 -- I get that Grace's campaign is the survival portion of the game, but RE9 made her out to be a wimp, and her campaign felt only marginally more substantial than DLC. And a final minor gripe: revisiting Raccoon City was. . . underwhelming. Not sure what I expected (it IS a bombed out-city, I guess), but it absolutely didn't meet the mark.

White Shadows is a disturbingly beautiful and dark cinematic adventure inspired by Orwell's and other dystopias.

The comparison to classics like Limbo, Inside and Little Nightmares is easy, both in terms of gameplay and mood, but this game brings a truly unique take on the genre. Features a sinister carnival and a very oppressive society, and comes with a very accurate warning about racism, animal violence, and other sensitive themes.

Positive

•  Great ambiance with polished noir aesthetics
•  Smooth controls of creature at different stages
•  Impressive camera work frames different perspectives around 2D movement
•  Suitable classical soundtrack + distorted gibberish vocals
•  Disturbingly beautiful and dark with moody lighting
•  Classic puzzle mechanics (crates, machinery, levers, some timing)

Negative

•  Expected bigger ending twist or climax

Gravelord is an old school first person shooter, but I'm not going to waste any time going into detail on the gameplay mechanics.

The mouse aim feels very stuttery, especially when moving the mouse diagonally, which makes the combat look and feel terrible. I mean, its technically playable as long as you don't ever try to circle strafe. 

Enemy variety, gun variety, map design, nothing matters because the most fundamental part of any FPS is completely broken and just not fun to play.

The graphics are amazing. 
The story so far seems interesting. 
The customisation is plentiful. 
I see people mentioning optimization issues but I have experienced none. 
I can see myself putting a lot of hours into this game.

Edit: I died on beskar mode and lost my save. "The heart will break, but broken live on".
After playing this game for around 6-7 hours and having no real issues. I can say it'll probably be one of my favourite games. 
My frames run around 50-60 fps but I do feel that single player story games can be enjoyed down to 30fps.
I've had a lot of fun with customising the characters, there's a lot to unlock. 
And there is a lot of content to play. 
Overall I do think Zero Company is a fun experience and I do recommend it to anyone who enjoys X-Com style games.
